chapter: Fish fries, passing the hat and district living
title: Why they called him Rat: passing the hat
summary: Dawson explains his nickname Rat, given by Alphonse Picou, because he was the one willing to pass the hat and could drop coins into his palm.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Yeah, that's what a nickname was called in Tar-kun. You see, my nickname used to be Rat.
Uh-huh.
They called me Rat them times.
Why do you call me Rat?

Well, uh, you see, I used to be sneaking around, you know. Steaking around with the women or the money? No, the money. Because it set me to collect money, I'd go, I'd make the rock going back in Tar-kun, take half of the money out there.
Yeah? That's why they call you Rat. Would you be playing with the band, or would you just be? Yeah, I'd play, I'd play. Well, you were the band leader.
Yeah, yeah, I was with them. And, um, but I was the only one that nobody would want to make no collection, you see. Oh, you were the only one.
Well, you went to pass the hat out. Yeah, I passed the hat.
Everybody was too important, they didn't want to pass the hat. But you weren't.
So you took some money out there, sir.
I said, I'll pass it, you know. Did you get more money? Man, I could take that cap like that at the bottom, and hit it at the bottom of me and caught it and jump out in my hand.
You got to tap it like that? You should have been a Jaguar.
I had more quarters in my hand than I had in the hat than I caught it.
You could have had the hat to the hole in the bottom. Yeah, yeah, they called me Rat.
I'd show up in there because Alphonse Pico was the one who started calling me Rat.
Oh, yeah? Yeah.
That's where you been at. I said, out there, and I had to go to the back there. Yeah, you went to the back there. Whatever I was given, they had to put it in the cigar box, you know.
Well, they never, did anybody else pass after that? No, nobody passed. They were always too important. No, they didn't.
They play all right, but nobody didn't want to get up and pass the hat. Yeah, when it come time, when it come time, you say, Rat, time for the hat, you know.
And they didn't even care that you were keeping it all right.
Oh, you all ain't interested. I'll be interested because I'm going to come back here with a dollar a half or two dollars in my pocket.
That was a common thing to pass the hat, the passage to you all the time.
